title: Mattock (North Sea Swamp)
summary: Mattock is connected with a swamp near North Sea in Southampton. The name appears in eighteenth-century local records and may preserve either a description of swampy land or a personal name.
history_content: The placename belongs to the North Sea landscape of Southampton, where lots, meadow, and swamp edges were described in local land materials. The adjoining land was also described as showing evidence of earlier Native habitation.
translation_content:
One possible interpretation is bad land, a fitting description for swamp ground. Another possibility is that the swamp was named for a Native person who formerly lived nearby.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names help us get around by providing an official reference for maps, and they also hold cultural information about the people who live there.”

— Geographical Names Board of Canada, The Geographical Names Board of Canada Celebrates 125 Years (2022), video transcript, opening explanation of place names

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
whereintheworld_content: Map location note: the pin is placed near North Sea in Southampton to represent a swamp location described in broad landscape terms in the source; it is not an exact swamp boundary.
